scope: Source ordering argument for the separately pinned archived controller. No new RTL, MC/PHY simulation, physical DDR validation or global reset/drain acknowledgment.

candidate.operation: After observing completion of the final acknowledged write request, stop new memory requests and issue a normal aligned single-beat AXI read to exactly that write request address. Observe its valid response, then obtain a fresh sticky ECC status snapshot.
candidate.address: The same 31-bit, 64-byte-aligned AWADDR of the final write; do not use an arbitrary scratch/read-only address.
candidate.inference: Under the assumptions below, the read cannot issue before the final write column command, which cannot issue before preceding ordered writes or before its RMW read returns. The rank write-to-read interlock and actual returned read data provide an observable ordering witness. This is a source-supported candidate, awaiting directed qualification against the real archived control/data path.
not_established: All PHY or maintenance queues empty.
Physical memory correctness or RK numerical equivalence.
assumptions: One exclusive memory owner on channel 0; no concurrent host/PCIe/JTAG or other-master memory traffic.
Exactly the pinned NORM ordering, single-rank, ECC-enabled controller profile; no changed ordering/address/clock parameters.
The existing single-outstanding, ID-zero, aligned 64-byte single-beat memory profile; no unsupported bursts, narrow accesses or channel-select truncation.
All earlier read responses have completed, every earlier write has received its B response, and no new write can enter after the recorded final write.
At least one write was issued, and the enclosing final 64-byte beat remains mapped, initialized and exclusively owned.
No reset, calibration/clock loss, timeout, AXI protocol/error response, ECC disable or status-clear race occurs between the job and the checked fence.
The subsequent monitor snapshot requires IRQ mask 3, ECC enabled, zero sticky CE/UE status and no concurrent monitor fault.

source_ordering_chain.statement: The generated profile is NORM, with four bank machines, one rank and BANK_ROW_COLUMN addressing. NORM orders write column commands; reads do not universally join that ordering queue.

B is pushed after the final native command acceptance, not physical retirement. The subsequent read is introduced only after this observed B; the shared native command pipeline preserves accepted command sequence before bank-machine allocation.
Read and write use the same byte-to-native address translator. Reusing the exact aligned final AWADDR preserves rank, bank, row and column decoding. Channel 0 has one rank.

Busy rank-bank comparisons place later requests behind existing requests to that rank-bank. Head advancement and open-bank transfer follow predecessor completion/column issue, rather than allowing a later same-bank read to bypass a pending RMW write.

Masked ECC writes select native WRITE_BYTES. They remain write requests for NORM ordering; their first column phase is a read. The state machine waits for the matching PHY RMW return before reasserting column readiness for the write phase.
Actual write column issue requires order_q_zero. The ordering queue advances only at non-RMW-read column issue, so issuance of the final write requires preceding ordered write columns to have issued.

The rank-control write-to-read timer starts from writes issued to that rank and derives its interval from CWL, burst length and nWTR. The bank-state read issue path checks that interlock and PHY FIFO readiness; this is not an arbitrary software wait.

RMW read errors are raw validity-qualified ECC events even though RMW returns do not produce normal UI read data. These events feed sticky ECC status while ECC is enabled. A preceding RMW read must have returned before its write phase can issue.

The fence read response is produced from physical read-return data through the ECC/UI read path and AXI data FIFO. The UI multiple-error bit is stored with the read beat and selects SLVERR; no write-data forwarding source was found on this inspected return path.

final_b_or_clean_ecc_status.statement: B is a command-acceptance response and the independent control-port status read has no memory retirement dependency. Neither alone supplies the required ordering witness.

arbitrary_address_read.statement: NORM allows reads to bypass the global write order. Only the same-rank-bank dependency on the final write supplies the additional link; an unrelated address is insufficient.

bank_idle.statement: Internal bank idle reflects queue ownership. A bank machine may finish and pass an open bank when its non-RMW-read column command is sent. That is not a public all-PHY-work-retired signal.

mc_read_idle.statement: mc_read_idle is derived from the column read FIFO being empty and calibration complete. It does not count write retirement and is not a public wrapper drain acknowledgment.

public_maintenance_ack.statement: The wrapper exposes maintenance acknowledgments, but the generated core hardwires self-refresh, refresh and ZQ requests to zero. They cannot be commanded as a fence through this existing interface.

next_source_implementation.component: A separate ordinary-AXI readback-fence sequencer below the unchanged raw command boundary, followed by the existing ECC monitor check.
next_source_implementation.ownership: Record the last accepted write address, track outstanding write completion, freeze new memory admission, and retain the final beat allocation until fence/error recovery finishes. Require audited exclusive ownership; do not turn B into a retirement counter.
next_source_implementation.failure_behavior: Hold pending AR until handshake, reject non-OKAY/nonzero-ID/missing-RLAST responses, quarantine on clock/calibration/reset uncertainty or timeout, and never publish successful job completion before the qualified fence and monitor snapshot.
next_source_implementation.controller_port_extension: No new MIG port is needed for this candidate because it uses the existing AXI read channel. It does not replace a separately audited whole-domain reset protocol.
required_qualification: Exercise actual pinned bank queue/compare/state and rank-control logic with writes spanning different banks and delayed RMW read returns; a hand-written echo slave alone cannot qualify the source ordering premise.
Demonstrate that a same-final-address read stays behind the final RMW write while an unrelated-bank read can complete early, preserving the negative control.
Cover same-row bank passing, different-row/precharge paths, prior writes to other banks, repeated final addresses, PHY-side backpressure and read-response stalls.
Bind the wrapper to unchanged raw BO replays and full output oracles after the ordering premise passes; do not replace commands with tensor operations.
Retain reset/calibration-loss/error and pending-channel expectations; do not manufacture a generic drained acknowledgment or successful memory initialization result.
